children: Group President and Head of Commercial Banking will step down on 30 September as the lender integrates commercial banking into its retail and institutional segments

Kotak Mahindra Bank Group President and Head of Commercial Banking Manish Kothari will step down from the lender on 30 September 2026, ending a 31-year association with the Kotak Group. Kothari submitted his resignation on 10 September and will leave at the close of business on 30 September.

Kothari has spent more than three decades with the organisation, including over 15 years in its core leadership team. According to the bank, he plans to pursue opportunities outside Kotak, including the possibility of launching an entrepreneurial venture.

In his resignation letter, Kothari said he had discussed his future plans with Managing Director and CEO Ashok Vaswani several months ago. He also said he had worked with the bank’s whole-time directors and business leaders to facilitate a smooth transfer of responsibilities.
Kothari’s departure comes as Kotak Mahindra Bank reorganises its commercial banking operations. The lender will no longer operate commercial banking as a standalone business under a separate head.
Instead, the portfolio will be integrated into the bank’s existing retail and institutional segments. The transition process has already commenced.
Kothari has led the commercial banking business since 2022, overseeing areas including agri finance, rural finance, logistics finance, infrastructure finance, microcredit and gold loans.
The exit comes amid wider leadership changes at Kotak Mahindra Bank. Earlier, Vaswani indicated that he would not seek reappointment after completing his current term on 31 December 2026.
Kothari’s departure marks another significant leadership transition for the lender as it prepares for changes to its senior management structure.

With commercial banking set to be absorbed into the broader retail and institutional segments, the bank’s focus will now shift to executing the integration while maintaining continuity across its lending and financing businesses.
Kothari’s exit also marks the departure of one of the Kotak Group’s longest-serving senior executives after more than three decades with the organisation.
